name: chemotaxis
title: Chemotaxis on a secreted, diffusing field
question:
Can the wrapper couple a secretion source, a finite-difference diffusion field, and
a chemotaxis response inside one CompuCell3D Process so that responder cells migrate
directionally on the resulting gradient?
hypothesis:
Source cells secreting a diffusible signal set up a spatial gradient; responder cells
with a chemotaxis term bias their motion up that gradient and migrate toward the
source region.
objective:
Run the secretion + diffusion + chemotaxis composite on an 80x80 lattice for 2000
Monte-Carlo steps through `CompuCell3DProcess`, exposing the concentration field in
the animated scene and reading population back through the output ports.
description:
A minimal chemotaxis slice: type-A source cells secrete a "Signal" field solved by the
wrapper's finite-difference diffusion step, and type-B responders chemotax up its
gradient. The run is a single real cc3d 4.6.0 trajectory. The committed scene overlays
the live concentration field on the cell lattice so the gradient and the response are
visible together.
claim:
The composite runs the real engine with an emergent, evolving concentration field and
drives net responder migration toward the source. Under this configuration the
responder population contracts over the run (45 -> 16 cells across 2000 MCS) as cells
move up-gradient — reported as observed, not as a tuned recruitment yield.
expected_behavior: A concentration gradient forms from the secreting source (visible in the scene overlay).
Responder cells move up the gradient toward the source.
Population changes over the run are reported honestly from the output ports.

behavior_tests.description:
The coupled secretion/diffusion/chemotaxis composite runs on cc3d 4.6.0 through the
single-Process wrapper, evolves a concentration field, and produces net up-gradient
responder migration (committed animated scene with field overlay + population chart).

limitations: Directional migration is shown qualitatively (animated scene with field overlay); a quantitative directional statistic (e.g. mean centroid displacement toward the source) is not computed here. The population attrition under this parameter set is reported as observed rather than tuned away.
